Character Story

<color=#ffd780>Character Story 2</color>
In the early days when Tatarasuna was still a prosperous place, the Wanderer walked amongst its people, going by the name "Kabukimono."
And the thing that ended his peaceful life was not all that important in the grand scale of Inazuma's history.
Change came to the place in the form of the Akame Clan and a mechanic from Fontaine named Escher. The two cooperated very closely to further improve forging quality, and in the process, Akame introduced Escher to Niwa, who was also from the three Isshin traditions.
Escher's arrival caused quite the stir for a time, for it was through his revolutionary new techniques that they were able to process Crystal Marrow in such a way that their forging efficacy and production were both increased.
But as time passed, anomalies emerged within the great central furnace in Tatarasuna. Black gas gathered within the furnace, and it would gradually affect the bodies of the craftspeople there. Forging and smelting were the foundations of life in Tatarasuna, but now they had become death itself.
And as the toll mounted, the great furnace further went out of control. None could get close to its core, and even stopping it became nigh impossible.
As the highest authority at Tatarasuna, Niwa was forced to enact an information blackout while sending people to Inazuma City to beg aid from Tenshukaku.
For some reason, however, those who took to the sea in ships never returned. Horror began seeping into the hearts of Tatarasuna's people.
The Kabukimono knew that Niwa needed the Raiden Shogun's aid, but did not know that this was the very year when she had successfully built the perfect puppet using parts of herself as material, thus handing over management of the nation to the Guardian of Eternity. He thus boarded a small boat and braved storm and rain to arrive at Tenshukaku, seeking an audience with the Shogun.
But she now dwelled in the Plane of Euthymia, and he was repeatedly refused. In desperation, he displayed the golden feather on his person and asked to see Yae Miko instead.
At this time, Miko was busy assisting the Guardian, and though she rushed down as soon as she heard this news, she could only meet the distressed Kabukimono briefly. Yet he had no ears for her promises to send people to their aid immediately, and returned in despair, convinced that the Shogunate had forsaken Tatarasuna.
Still, the dispatch was sent, the people were mobilized, and they crossed by sea. Yet they arrived to no great disaster. Indeed, most people knew nothing of what had happened. It was the mechanic, Escher, who explained that Niwa had fled with his family for fear of punishment for his malfeasance, and that the Kabukimono had gone into the core zone in his place, shutting the furnace down.
Receiving word that the Kabukimono had been friends with the fleeing Niwa, Yae guessed at the heaviness in his heart and did not wish to further disturb him, merely sending someone to return the feather to him.
Later still, he would disappear without a trace from Tatarasuna. But as people reminisced, they could never forget the celebratory dance he had performed together with them on the day that Mikoshi Nagamasa successfully forged his great blade.
His steps fluttered lightly like a feather in the wind then, and they could not have known that he, like a feather, would depart from them and journey to places unknown.
<color=#ffd780>Character Story 4</color>
The sixth of Snezhnaya's Fatui Harbingers is known as The Balladeer.
And yet this name was not his to own from the start. Indeed, they were yet separated by over a hundred years.
After leaving Inazuma, he forsook the name Kabukimono, reverting to his nameless state, and did not even consider taking another until The Jester found him.
In the end, such titles as "puppet" or "Kabukimono" were all given to him by mortals. And since he would no longer have them as companions, there was no point in using the names they gave him.
But The Jester proved most persuasive, and the puppet was intrigued by the frenzied banquet he spoke of, and so accompanied the man to Snezhnaya to serve in the Fatui.
A stranger named The Doctor would welcome him warmly in this frigid northern land, inviting the Wanderer to be the key reference material in his experiments — his grand research project.
Puppet-making techniques had their roots in Khaenri'ah, and his nature as a creation of the Electro Archon made him all the more special. The Doctor was fascinated by this field of study, and, using the Wanderer as a foundational blueprint, would perform research and experiments for several decades before finally attaining the techniques that would go on to form the basis for his Segments.
In return, The Doctor would unlock the seal on his body, causing his abilities to greatly increase, to the point where he was a match for the lower-ranked Harbingers.
But even so, he did not choose another name. His colleagues called him the "puppet," and so he saw himself also — a puppet, unafraid of death and inexhaustible.
On the Tsaritsa's orders, he would lead a company to explore the Abyss, and there he spent much time. More than once he was wounded, then repaired by The Doctor, and thus he grew stronger, surviving to be wounded again by ever mightier foes.
Much later, he would bring the results of his exploration back to Snezhnaya, gaining the sixth seat in the process. His orders were also changed. Instead of exploring the Abyss, he was now to constantly be on standby, assisting the clandestine activities of the Fatui across the world.
And it was only then that he felt that that new name, "The Balladeer," fit him.
<color=#ffd780>Character Story 5</color>
The many things that happened after that might even be called soul-stirring, but for the fact that few now remember them.
Only those who witnessed those events would keep them as legends in their hearts, and so they continue to quietly exist, as ancient songs lost to the world.
Within Irminsul, The Balladeer came into contact with the "truth" that Lesser Lord Kusanali had placed within the flow of information. This secret had been hidden within one of The Doctor's many hearts, and just as she claimed, this truth in first person contained all his remaining honesty.
And thus did The Balladeer come to know of past truths: Niwa, who had taught him how to live like an ordinary human and treated him like one, had not fled Tatarasuna to escape punishment as Escher had claimed. In fact, the true culprit had been Escher — no, The Doctor — all along. And as for the heart that had been placed within The Balladeer, it had been cut, still warm, from Niwa's breast.
This death had been nicely packaged within an incident at the forge, and such was Escher's silvered tongue that he all too quickly convinced everyone that this was due to the failings of the local overseer.
As the next person in charge, Mikoshi Nagamasa would have faced capital punishment if not for the intervention of his loyal samurai retainer, Katsuragi, who willingly took the burden of wrongdoing upon himself.
The tragedy that followed need not be elaborated upon. Nagamasa, unwilling as he was, had to wash the stain from the Mikoshi name, and could not allow himself to die here.
And so he brought forth his beloved blade, the Daitatara Nagamasa, and struck Katsuragi down in a single blow, the blade cutting so deep that it nearly split the slain man in twain...
...And had they not all believed in their god?
Why then, did they have to face such a calamity?
If the enigmatic puppet they called the Kabukimono had never existed, would Escher have done the same thing there?
Even if the chance were infinitesimal, could the tragedy of Tatarasuna have been salvaged?
Anyone anywhere else in this world would be able to do nothing about this, but not The Balladeer. He knew that he alone could attempt this one thing, here and now.
He believed himself bold, for he feared not death. Death was but a tiny threat to a puppet, and only humans with hearts knew horror.
He also knew himself to be craven, and for that he had remorse. If he had been then more like he was at present... if he had learned to be less trusting... Would those he had viewed as friends have met such a ruinous end?
Traitor, hero, god, discarded detritus — all these identities would cease to matter to one who leaped into the flux.
The information flow was a place of incomparable silence, and yet his blood roiled in his ears, and his mind roared.
Embrace oblivion!
The puppet was a discarded milksop, the Kabukimono unaccomplished and sheltered, and Scaramouche was a schemer — one who eventually went against divine decree, seeking to go against the tides of the world.
But what of it?
Once upon a time, these inhuman hands had shut a great blazing furnace without caring if his ten fingers were burned to a crisp.
Now, these hands grasped at the tiniest possibility, twisting the truth to fulfill his wish.
Yes, embrace it, embrace it with this form that shall be obliterated!
To ruin with this life, as worthless as flowers and feathers and the dawn dew!
Farewell, world! The future shall be what it will. Farewell nonetheless!

<color=#ffd780>Character Story 2</color>
When Columbina first came to the Fatui, she immediately found them very different from the Frostmoon Scions.
No one seemed to make unreasonable demands of her. No one appeared to desire anything from her or revere her — at least, not on the surface.
The concept of "colleagues" was new to her, too. Within it, she sensed something both unfamiliar and deeply appealing: a sense of equality, occasionally mixed with a familiar notion of "trade." She was still learning to navigate this way of life.
The first to approach her was The Doctor. Columbina could hear admiration in this colleague's words — not the same as worship; at least, it was based on the premise of equality.
"If you don't mind, could you help me with a small task?" the colleague asked politely.
Help? She had expected this to be something she was obliged to give in return, but here, she actually had a choice. Or perhaps it was this very colleague who was offering her the choice.
Even though The Doctor's words carried a faint echo of something ominous, like distant thunder from a far-off storm, the sense of having a choice was undeniably satisfying.
At first, everything went smoothly. The Doctor's lab was filled with all sorts of strange devices, and Columbina only needed to lightly apply her power here, manipulate that there, and everything would work out.
"Not bad. You did very well."
Columbina liked praise. It was new to her, a novel experience.
But before long, compliments shifted to "Not quite enough," "You can do better," or "You're capable of more..."
Suddenly, Columbina realized that what The Doctor was seeing wasn't her, but some version of what she should be, or the level her powers should reach. It reminded her of the days before she had joined the Fatui...
She felt a pang of sadness. Did anyone else ever feel sad just for being themselves? She didn't know if others felt that, but she did.
It wasn't that she wanted to become what others expected, but that what they saw wasn't her. The real her, like an unwelcome child at a party, was left alone on the sidelines...
<color=#ffd780>Tri-Lunar Convergence</color>
After acquiring tri-lunar authority, Columbina naturally had some questions:
Could this power really do everything? What should she use it for?
She felt that the things she wanted to do were almost all within the reach of the three moons' power: Moving freely between the moon and Teyvat, effortlessly transporting herself and other objects, making flowers bloom more brilliantly, causing fruits to grow fuller...
She even tried to wake Sandrone up. But that was one of the few things this trilunar power could not accomplish for her.
As for everything else, she either didn't want to do it, or she felt that she shouldn't.
What she loved was the way this world and her home looked now. Changing it at will just because she could, molding its appearance and rules to suit her own whims... She felt that would be wrong. No matter how good her intentions, doing so would make her no different from The Doctor, she felt.
She regarded this world as her "home," not as her possession, and there was a great difference between the two.
So she offered a portion of her power, that it may continue to protect this beautiful home as it always had. The part she kept for herself needed only to allow her to live happily with her friends, as before, and to guard what she cherished when necessary.
In that moment, Columbina suddenly understood the choices her three elder sisters had made. Rather than seeking to "rule," what they had wanted most was simply to "protect" this world beneath the moon.
Could she say that she was their little sister, after all? The thought brought a sweet sense of harmony.
It felt almost like an inherited trait, or perhaps a "family tendency" moon goddesses had.
A warm feeling rose in Columbina's heart at the thought. She seemed to have again discovered something she had longed for:
The bonds and legacy shared among family.

Nahida, using the Gnosis of a foreign land as leverage, deprived the cunning foe of his "segments" as insurance.
But the enemy immediately requested for a bargain as well, offering up critical knowledge of the world's "truth."
His knowledge of the values rooted in this land was without peer, and thus had he intended to take advantage of Nahida's curiosity and sense of responsibility from the very beginning. Indeed, the way he saw it, there could be no bargaining chip more suitable than knowledge.
With one Gnosis still in her hands, Nahida could not help but hesitate. She barely knew more about the Gnoses than she knew the "truth" of the world.
The Gnosis, to her, was but a core that gathers a mass of elemental power at her discretion. But if there is nothing more to a Gnosis, why was a god so eager to gather all of them together?
Shaking hands in bargain means an equal compromise for both sides, a far cry from any victory. On the other hand, turning down the bargain indicates a certain type of "ignorance," which, obviously, would more easily invite a loss of control.
Thus did the "God of Wisdom" instantly find her answer...
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the Electro Gnosis</color>
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : All right, that's enough conversation for today. The experiment is over and it's time to tidy up the equipment and reclaim any useful materials.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : For example... the Gnosis.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Lesser Lord Kusanali, you're an intelligent archon. I'm sure you understand the disparity in our combat abilities at this time...
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Besides, you have no way to use that Electro Gnosis in battle.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Didn't you say you were here to negotiate with me? Somehow it's starting to seem like you intend to take it by force now.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Hahaha... I'm merely stating a fact.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : After all, I'm also a scholar. Naturally, I hope to show proper respect and dignity to the God of Wisdom.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Your hypocrisy is built on absolute confidence.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : I understand your scheme, but...
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : ...What if I were to destroy the Gnosis now, and awaken the Heavenly Principles?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Awaken... the heavenly principles?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Do you think that's really possible?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : The Heavenly Principles have been silent for many years, but the Gnoses are symbols of their control over Teyvat and all the laws...
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Will the destruction of a Gnosis attract the attention of the Heavenly Principles? And if so... how do the Fatui plan to deal with the consequences?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Do you dare... to gamble such a possibility with me?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Hmph, "gamble"? How surprising.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I thought you would show evidence or use rigorous reasoning to prove your point... The word "gamble" is the last thing I expected to hear from the God of Wisdom.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : But this is a clever move. You must have seen through me when I first captured your consciousness.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : As a scholar, I respect all possibilities. This has always been my principle and is an essential trait as an experimenter.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Indeed, I can't ignore this possibility. So tell me then, what are your conditions?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : This foreign Gnosis will only lead to disaster if it stays in Sumeru...
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : But this Electro Gnosis is the prize I obtained after defeating one of your fellow Harbingers.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Now, as the one who initiated this cascade of events, shouldn't you pay the corresponding price?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Price? Interesting. What price would you have me pay?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : ...How about erasing all your other segments?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Hahaha... So this is how you wish to restrict me, the most threatening opponent of the Nation of Wisdom. What you request of me is like plucking out the eyes I have placed in the dimension of time.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Segments are extraordinarily difficult to make. They require extremely rare resources and enormous amounts of time and effort. Requiring me to destroy them all here and now... Bravo, a suitably wise decision on your part.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Yes, how very interesting... Can I assume that you have long been wary of me?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Among all the versions of me, this segment you see now is the most selfish. If it weren't me, your idea wouldn't have worked.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : What did you see when you were imprisoned? You were observing me, and that's how you know I've long grown tired of their doubts and endless arguments.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Like you said, it's difficult to make peace with yourself.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Being as smart as you are, have you managed to do that?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I see. If you think all those versions of me are worth a Gnosis... Then, deal.
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : You sure didn't hesitate much. Is the relationship between all the versions of you really that bad?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I don't think there's any need to dwell on that. The surplus versions of me can be exchanged for a Gnosis. Do you think anyone can offer themselves at a higher price?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Besides, with my abilities, it's only a matter of time until I find better "perspectives." Perhaps it's best to say... you're just temporarily ahead.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : But what I'd like to know is, how can you be sure that I've really erased them?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : I can see your remaining honesty...
<color=#ffd780>About the Dendro Gnosis</color>
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Another chess piece... And where is your Dendro Gnosis?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : ...Don't be greedy, Harbinger of Snezhnaya.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : No, this is a different transaction. If you intend to turn off the Akasha anyway, then there's no further use for the Gnosis of Sumeru, is there?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Besides, isn't it the archon's duty to deliver what's desired of the seeker?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Oh? Judging from your expression, you don't seem to find the idea very agreeable. Then let's think of it this way... Since you're the God of Wisdom, how about I exchange some knowledge with you?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : People exchanging knowledge with the God of Wisdom is the stuff of legends, yet here you wish to exchange knowledge for the God of Wisdom's property...
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : Arrogant as that is, it has piqued my interest.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Let me ask you... Have you in all your mighty knowledge ever heard the rumor that "the skies of Teyvat are fake"?
<color=#37ffff>Buer</color> : ...Huh?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : That's the secret hidden by Irminsul concerning the "truth" of this world...
<color=#ffd780>About The Doctor</color>
Actually, it's very smart of the Traveler to be wary of me right now. After all, The Doctor has shown that his technology can apparently even control human minds...
When you left, I was still in the middle of restoring everyone's minds. Thankfully, when The Doctor mentioned "depositing information into the subconscious," he didn't mean engraving information into their minds...
...Instead, he did something closer to creating hallucinations. That was still within my power to fix.
Luckily, I managed to finish my restorations and mind-jump away from him just as he was about to capture me.
I gave away my true identity when I restored everyone's minds, which means we've lost another one of our trump cards.
Also... The Doctor is already an expert at modifying Akasha Terminals. Maybe it's only a matter of time until he captures my consciousness inside the Akasha.

customize.name: Collei

customize.text: Voice-Over

<color=#ffd780>More About Collei: III</color>
I was once taken to someone they call "The Doctor" for treatment for my Eleazar... well, actually "treatment" is the wrong word — it was more... experimentation. After so long in that place, I couldn't help but start to wonder, what have I done wrong to deserve this? Why won't anyone come to rescue me? Gradually, I went from hating just the Fatui to hating everyone in the world. Thinking about it now... it was quite childish.

customize.name: Tighnari
customize.desc: A young researcher well-versed in botany who currently serves as a Forest Watcher in Avidya Forest. He is a straight shooter with a warm heart - and a dab hand at guiding even the dullest of pupils.

customize.text: Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About Collei</color>
Anyway, the person who eventually rescued Collei and brought her to me for care said that she had been given to a Harbinger known as "The Doctor."
I have no idea how this "Doctor" managed to do it, but her case of Eleazar was completely stable for all the years that Collei was with them.
However, Collei's days with the Fatui were anything but pleasant.
Collei is a resilient individual and always tries to appear cheerful, but her experience with the Fatui has left deep scars. Even now, she can still feel deathly afraid of someone touching her.
<color=#ffd780>About Haypasia</color>
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Hmph... so you mean, you're leaving this place soon?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Indeed. Otherwise, we could have perhaps talked a little more.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I was just about to set out when I remembered something important. To that end, I made a final trip to Pardis Dhyai.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Let me ask... have you been taking care of a scholar by the name of Haypasia?
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Your sources are accurate, no doubt because you have recruited many informants, but you are right, Haypasia has indeed been receiving treatment from me.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Forgive me for asking, but how's the treatment coming along?
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Given the way you're asking, I assume you have something to say?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Since you asked, I'll be frank: I would like to take Haypasia to Snezhnaya.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : It's incredibly difficult to transfer a patient. As a scholar yourself, shouldn't you at least be aware of this?
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Oh? I can't believe your utter lack of faith in me, to the point of even questioning my general level of knowledge. How unbefitting.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Well, you're the only one who's ever made such a request.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I have my ways of keeping her safe during the journey. In addition, I can also promise that under my care, Haypasia will receive the most advanced and effective treatment.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I will personally supervise her treatment and see to her recovery. Would that be agreeable to you?
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Haypasia was born in Sumeru, and remains a scholar of the Akademiya. Her situation has not become dire enough to necessitate her transfer to another nation.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Transporting her to Snezhnaya is risky, and the potential benefits are unknown. As the person currently responsible for her treatment, I cannot possibly sign off on this transfer.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Your suggestion is rude and reckless. I'll pass.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : I see, I see. Of course, your opinion makes perfect sense.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Hehe... You're still young, but already quite stubborn. I must say, you are not like what I had expected...
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Under normal circumstances, I wouldn't just let you off the hook like this, but unfortunately, I'm in a hurry today — what with Her Most Noble Majesty, the Tsaritsa, calling for our return.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : Luckily, there is still some time left for me to take care of everything before I leave.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : It's just as the Akademiya said — you're a responsible and gifted scholar. Sadly, even with all of that, you're still lacking a bit of shrewdness.
<color=#37ffff>Dottore</color> : And that's also why people like you can never realize that sooner or later, everyone must pay the price for what they've learned.
<color=#ffd780>About Dottore</color>
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Have you ever met The Doctor?
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Yes, I know him.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : Actually, he left Pardis Dhyai just a little while ago.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : The Harbinger you mentioned came to me because he wanted to take the scholar Haypasia away with him.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : I don't know much about The Doctor. But after talking with him, I realized that just like many other scholars, he possesses an aura of arrogance that I've come to detest.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : It's not so much that he's looking down on others, but more that he's confident in himself and his abilities to a point of near insanity.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : I would never refer a patient to someone like him.
<color=#37ffff>Tighnari</color> : I prepared myself for a protracted battle of wits, and was really surprised to see him just give up on the topic. Still, his reaction really concerned me...
The Doctor's Subordinate
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About The Doctor</color>
He's... building something — ambitious doesn't even begin to describe it. Feels like this could be the big one. God knows how long he's been planning it...
A while back, he told us he'd be returning to Snezhnaya. We weren't expecting him back so soon... This time, he brought some gemstones with him, or something. Two of them.
Back when this all started, the higher-ups dispatched three units to Nod-Krai to execute their plan. They were led by The Doctor, Marionette, and The Damselette respectively.
I was part of the The Damselette's unit to begin with.
She never interacted with us much. In fact, she seemed sorta... detached from everything. Not because she was distracted, it just felt like she was indifferent to the world around her. Like she had no stake in anything that happened.
She always seemed like she was staring off into the distance. Almost as if she didn't see anything worth living for in the present, so she had to look further afield... Ah, that's right — she always used to stare up at the sky.
The Doctor used to stand nearby and watch her. Apparently, they got along well at first. But somewhere along the way, she grew wary of him, and started avoiding him as much as possible.
After she left, everyone in our unit merged with The Doctor's. He's... similarly indifferent to the world — except when it comes to the moons. He seems to have big plans for them.
Right now, obtaining the three moons is his number one priority. He even said... if he can only get his hands on two of them, he'll create a third one himself.
Mercanaries
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the Akademiya</color>
The Akademiya is working on an important and potentially world-changing project. They are creating a new god... a god that will belong to them, and to the people of Sumeru.
It may seem as if Sumeru's academics are thriving, but ever since the death of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, scholarly breakthroughs have been few and far between.
The withering of Irminsul has been getting worse recently. The sages have tried everything they could think of, but nothing's worked. I'm always hearing them say things like, "If only Greater Lord Rukkhadevata was still with us..."
And then, someone from the Fatui showed up. They called him "The Doctor"... He brought a... a "Gnosis," and said he wanted to borrow the Akademiya's research facilities.
The Doctor was previously expelled from the Akademiya. At first, the sages looked down at him in disdain... But when he said those words, everyone's expression changed.
He asked them: "Do you wish to create a god?"
First, the Akademiya spent a long time constructing a "divine vessel," which was based on an exquisite humanoid puppet.
After that, they harvested dreams via the Sabzeruz Festival samsara, maximizing the Akasha's output...
With The Doctor's help, and the Akasha now functioning at maximum efficiency, they were able to use it to extract the power from the Gnosis and convert it into a "divine core."
Next, they decided that their new god needed to possess "divine wisdom." For that to happen... they needed a huge quantity of Divine Canned Knowledge.
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About Sumeru</color>
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Heh. Have you heard? It seems that the Sumeru Akademiya has made a real mess of one of their big projects!
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : The Six Darshans have been left leaderless as a result, which has forced the weak Dendro Archon to take over.
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Wait, so do you mean that something terrible has happened?
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Terrible? No, not at all. It's wonderful news, in fact!
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : I've heard that Lord Dottore managed to infiltrate Sumeru during the chaos and perform a great work in the Tsaritsa's name with almost no effort at all!
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Huh... Then what about Lord Scaramouche? I've heard that he was recently seen in Sumeru as well...
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Lord Scaramouche? Ah, you mean the one with the famously bad temper? To be honest, I've heard that he hasn't been seen since his assignment in Inazuma.
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Are you suggesting that he might be related to the project in Sumeru as well?
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : I'm not sure, really. But it seems that a lot of the soldiers under his command have been transferred elsewhere...
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Huh. Hmm... Well, you know, transfers happen all time, so who knows if those things are related at all?
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Anyway, I doubt that this will take away anything from the results that Lord Dottore has gotten this time!
<color=#ffd780>About Sumeru</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>(After completing the Archon Quest Interlude Chapter: Act III - Inversion of Genesis)</color>
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Heh. Have you heard? It seems that the Sumeru Akademiya has made a real mess of one of their big projects!
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : The Six Darshans have been left leaderless as a result, which has forced the weak Dendro Archon to take over.
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Wait, so do you mean that something terrible has happened?
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Terrible? No, not at all. It's wonderful news, in fact!
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : I've heard that Lord Dottore managed to infiltrate Sumeru during the chaos and perform a great work in the Tsaritsa's name with almost no effort at all!
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Is that so... Just as expected from the Second Harbinger...
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Huh? You don't seem happy, judging by your tone.
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : It is indeed good that the Harbinger succeeded, but I'm reminded that Lady Signora also succeeded at Inazuma only to...
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Look at you. You're worrying too much. From how I see it, we don't have many people, and that's fine.
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : With someone as powerful as Lord Dottore among our ranks, it shouldn't matter if the rest of our seats remain empty.
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : But enough about the Eighth Harbinger. It is said that the Sixth Harbinger's seat has been left vacant for hundreds of years. Is that not cause for concern?
<color=#ffd780>About Nod-Krai</color>
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Hey, have you heard? Something serious has happened with the higher-ups...
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Ah... you mean what happened with The Doctor and Marionette, right?
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : *sigh* For this to happen just as the
was about to kick off...
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : Look at you, worrying over nothing again, aren't you?
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : The Jester and The Rooster are leading the charge on that front. There's no way it could fail.
<color=#37ffff>Mikhail</color> : No matter what happens in Nod-Krai, it won't affect Her Majesty the Tsaritsa's great endeavor. We need only carry out our duties and wait to sing the praises of her farsighted wisdom, you'll see!
<color=#37ffff>Lyudmila</color> : Hmm... I hope things really do go smoothly over in Snezhnograd...
Trofin Snezhevich
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the order</color>
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : House of the Hearth is a shelter founded by "The Knave." Children raised in the House aren't related, but our bonds are tighter than blood.
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : After coming of age, those with potential undergo training to become agents, then infiltrate different locations to await orders. Unfortunately, I was deemed as "having potential."
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : What is your order?
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : Capture Aranara. It's an order from "The Doctor," so that he can study the connections between Aranara, dreams, and The Withering.
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : Weaponizing dreams and The Withering seems to be one of his projects. Of course, I and every Fatuus you defeated are his "source of study."
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : We can't see Aranara, but Kavus, Sudabeh, and Iotham have what it takes to befriend them.
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : So you let the Fatui abduct them to lure the Aranara out.
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : Correct, and the Aranara did show up. But their power truly was amazing, able to free those kids right under the nose of heavy security...
<color=#37ffff>Trofin Snezhevich</color> : The Doctor has eyes on something truly incredible this time...
Elchingen
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the Fungi Tournament</color>
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : So, this whole tournament... It was just an elaborate ploy to get other people to capture Fungi for you! And now you're gonna make them all into your evil minions!
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : Very impressive, you hit all the key notes there. I hold the tournament a few times, build up an army of Fungi living amongst the people... and then I can create all kinds of damage. You have to understand, this is a huge opportunity for me.
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : My accomplishments will eclipse those of all my other comrades. And then, my dear master Dottore, who left because of you, will finally realize that I can still be worth something to him...
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : You've worked for Dottore before...
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : But now... I think I might go one step further.
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : Getting rid of you would be doing a major service for all the Fatui, from the foot-soldiers to the harbingers. This could be a career-making moment for me... I'll finally earn Master Dottore's respect...
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : I'll just say it was a tragic accident. You placed too much trust in the Fungi, tried to push past the limits, and ended up causing the whole arena to collapse with you still inside.
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : Once this domain's sealed off, no one will ever find you. I'll have Kautilya assume all liability and criminal charges, then inform the Akademiya.
<color=#37ffff>Elchingen</color> : After that, I'll invest even more into this tournament, in the name of honoring your memory. I'll promote it harder, the competitions will be bigger and more frequent...
Clervie
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the House of the Hearth</color>
Although... after you hear all this, I think you might regret that decision.
Everyone in this family is nothing more than a tool, something to be used and exploited. We're all expendable... including me.
As long as you're useful, you get to stick around. Lose your value... and you're handed over to The Doctor, experimented on, and given a fate worse than death. I've seen it happen again and again, and I've had enough.

customize.name: Lyney
customize.desc: A famed Fontainian magician who possesses great stage presence as well as gift of the gab. Audiences are enthralled by his exquisite skills, and they hang on to his every clever word.

customize.text: Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About the House of the Hearth</color>
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Have The Knave and The Doctor ever worked together?
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : We met The Doctor back in Sumeru. He's super dangerous! And he's done all sorts of bad things!
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : ...It's possible that "Father" and The Doctor have had certain dealings, but I don't think "Father" would work with him.
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : We're not really on the same side, so there's not a lot of trust between them. That doesn't exactly set the stage for a successful partnership.
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : I did hear, though, that when "Father" first became a Harbinger, The Doctor offered to work with the House of the Hearth.
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : "Father" rejected most of his proposals, except for one... It had to do with some sort of secret experiment.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Secret experiment? Could that be what Clervie was talking about?
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : I don't think so...
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : I don't know any details about the experiment itself, but I do know it's an entirely independent operation. The Doctor only proposed a direction for the research. That was the extent of his involvement. I still don't think that counts as working together.
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : The details of the experiment are confidential, but complete records are kept on all participants. That doesn't seem to be the case with the situation Clervie referred to.
<color=#37ffff>Lyney</color> : I know you don't agree with some of the Fatui's methods, and I'm not asking you to. But, I am asking you to trust us on this. The House of the Hearth has its own principles. There are certain lines we're not willing to cross.

Experimental Subject: Acute Toxicity Test
Specimen 1: Male, 43 years
Specimen Presentation: Obese with signs of mental confusion. Vital signs were stable. Toxicology screening indicated the presence of other drugs in specimen's system.
Route of Administration: High-dose oral ingestion
Reactions: Specimen exhibited minor extremity spasms within 60 seconds, with no vomiting or distress in the chest area. Onset of hallucinations occurred at T+5 minutes, accompanied by cognitive-linguistic disorganization. Progression to respiratory failure and death occurred at T+8 minutes.
Specimen 2: Male, 28 years
Specimen Presentation: Medium build with signs of psychological instability. Physical restraints were utilized due to acute non-compliance. Vital signs were excessively robust, exceeding expected physiological parameters.
Route of Administration: High-dose gastric gavage
Reactions: Specimen reported numbness in the extremities, with neither spasms in the limbs nor vomiting. At T+2 minutes, subcutaneous bleeding was observed. An overwhelming sense of unfamiliarity comes over you the moment you touch the tree marrow, though you cannot quite pinpoint the source of this estrangement. It is as if you are thinking and standing still at the same time. You sense information quietly entering your mind while other data surfaces, both in a way that renders them in their most easily readable form.
It then dawns on you: this flood of information comes from Irminsul, taking the form of digitized memories. However, you feel neither irritation nor excitement. The data simply flows through your mind like water, and you observe it all with total calm and equanimity.
...
I should attend this meeting, I told my "self." Truth be told, not a single one of my "selves" occupies a critical position in my world, for the ample proliferation of my myriad selves ensures a perpetual surplus of manpower ready to dispose of whatever trivialities might crop up in this world.
Twenty-five-year-old "me" cast a sidelong glance at me, let out a cold laugh, and walked away. It is impossible to define the principles by which "we" are ordered or ranked, in truth, there is no formal hierarchy between us. However, the mere adoption of the epithet "Doctor" immediately establishes a relationship of superiors and subordinates with the other individuals in the organization.
I headed to that secret meeting, where Pierro explained the details of that so-called "false sky."
To me, the revelation of that false sky is of little consequence — I have no use for it, not while my hands are full of far more pressing research. That being said, the question of what lies beyond that sky is a curiosity worth pondering.
I recorded the details and told Pierro quite frankly that perhaps, one day, these secrets could be exchanged for even more useful commodities. Pierro offered a rather non-committal chuckle, while Pantalone signaled his agreement with my appraisal without saying a single word otherwise. As for Pulcinella, he mumbled a few choice phrases — mostly regarding some confidentiality agreement.
I had no interest in explaining myself further. That day will eventually come, sooner or later.
...
The deficit in live specimen data in this phase of the new drug trial has been substantial.
I suppose a shift in experimental focus is necessary, even if it requires the task of persuading myself to comply.
The lifespan of humans is far too fleeting, and their physical vessels altogether too fragile. Fantasies of immortality are so common merely because people remain pathetically trapped by their own limitations.
...
It has been some time since my return from Sumeru — from that operation where I lost "me," "myself," and "I," among others. A suitable reduction in burden does wonders for the mood. Besides, the two Gnoses I secured are bound to please the Tsaritsa.
At Zapolyarny Palace, I encountered Sandrone and Columbina. Though they are frequently seen in each other's company, they invariably maintain a distance of a few paces between them. As I walked past them, Sandrone let out a short scoff.
I presented the battle trophies during my audience with the Tsaritsa. I also informed her that I have given certain secrets to the Lord of Dendro in exchange, as a necessary expenditure. That Pulcinella, who usually has so much to say about keeping secrets, remained uncharacteristically silent today. Pantalone, too, offered no objection, content to serve as little more than a decorative vase at the proceedings. While the other Harbingers were not in attendance, they will hear of this soon enough.
Even the Lesser Lord Kusanali was once moved by the secrets Pierro holds. Four Descenders have come to Teyvat, and the third was erased for violating the one rule, though the method of that erasure remains a mystery.
As for the other three, I needed only to utter their numbers for her to understand immediately. The pensive silence that followed on her part was quite telling, really — it must surely stem from her relationship with that fourth Descender...
...
A friend of mine believes that my selfishness is not limited to others, but also aimed at myself in a manner that has long since transcended conventional definitions. (He did, subsequently, realize that he had spoken out of turn.) But pedestrian notions like "convention" mean absolutely nothing when one is addressing a member of the Fatui.
I find the operating room wonderfully serene, blissfully free from the incessant disturbances of my Segments. It is a place where I can enjoy a moment of ease, and reflect on myself... to an appropriate degree, of course.
Splitting the soul is not the most formidable obstacle. The next issue I must address is the mechanism of transfer, to ensure that the soul reaches its designated location.
First, we conquer the living world. Then, we head to the world beyond death.
I expect to begin with animal experiments. We can use the souls of others as the subjects of our experiments.
...
Phase Two of the soul experiment is concluded, with losses staying below projections. Evidently, the channel of transfer is more critical than the total volume.
Digitization... That's a splendid idea.
...
I perceive a truly magnificent scene: one half of my soul enters the Ley Lines through death, while the remaining half is injected as pure data. My two halves would then navigate those pathways to converge with the information of the past. It would be possible for me, in this manner, to achieve the preservation of my memories.
We might consider that as one of death's rare oversights.
Something that is even more eternal than eternal life itself?
Hehe... An immortal record would certainly satisfy that definition, of course.
...
You catch the faint sound of laughter, and like a thunderclap, it jolts your awareness back to the surface, pulling it free from the memories that nearly buried it. You let go of the tree marrow abruptly and wipe your face. You expect to find sweat, but there is none — it's all an illusion.
You try to trace the contours of this rather indistinct sensation, but it feels almost impossible. Morality and purpose, benevolence and malice... All that was originally good and virtuous within you is resisting every perception from those memories that don't belong to you. After an indeterminate amount of time — perhaps seconds, or perhaps minutes — you finally get a hold of yourself and put this unusual object away into your pack.

value.desc:
Reviled far and wide as a heretic, The Doctor — Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers — has seized the authority of the three moons and now ascends the long steps toward the divine throne of the "new world."
All should have belonged to us.
But reason cast out all that exceeded its limits, leaving humanity blind to its true nature.
Life and death bound us into mortal shells, shackling every spark of aspiration.
Time and space closed in last of all, fencing the mind into meek obedience, so no one would dare imagine breaking free.
From that point on, false gods governed the world, each one declaring their own truth as the sole, unassailable gospel — though none deserved the mantle they so loudly coveted.
There is no inherent structure to life's flow — order was merely imposed upon it. Strip away every shackle laid across this world, and the essence of all things will at last come into view.
And that revelation... is the first light of the new world.
"How much longer will you continue to suffer this stagnant, obsolescent world?"

value.name: Il Dottore
value.desc:
To push his heretical experiments to their end, Dottore has severed the constraints of his corporeal form. Now, he has merged as one with the Irminsul that threads through all of Teyvat.
This world inherently predates any natural order.
Until it cast its gaze, the origin and terminus of all matter were indeterminate.
Yet the weak, seeking to escape the crushing weight of freedom, would rather bow before the throne of "Certainty."
Only those with the resolve to pierce the veil of mundane perception may earn the right to forge a "new world."
That is the domain of "Possibility" — a perpetual and magnificent experiment that shall never reach its end.
It's time to enliven this stagnant, unchanging reality...
"How can you be certain that I am not capable of perfecting it?"
